constraints: Source archives must select the published consumer tests and their pinned project inputs together; peer-owned source bytes must remain unchanged.
Bounded metadata-only local verification: no archive build, full clone, device, network schema lookup or runtime dependency change.
alternatives: Setuptools MANIFEST.in explicit selection with a bounded FileList regression check.
Hatchling build include/exclude and force-include configuration.
Meson-python source-distribution selection through Meson packaging.
Dhall-generated manifest configuration with typed reusable declarations.
rationale: KEEP the native declarative manifest and correct twelve omissions: eleven pinned producer/contract files and the passport fixture README. The real Setuptools selector initially omits twelve of twenty-two required inputs and selects all twenty-two after the correction.

Hatchling offers file selection and Meson-python supports a native-build-oriented backend. Both still require explicit coverage of these consumer inputs; neither is shown to infer the published fixture dependencies. No native compilation or archive throughput requirement favors a backend migration for this component.

Dhall can express reusable typed configuration, but no shared generation requirement is present. The finite selection is directly expressible in the backend input; extra generation supplies no demonstrated selection correctness advantage.

A dedicated hosted step uses Setuptools 84.0.0, matching the Python 3.13 build configuration. Its FileList API is a backend-specific test dependency, not a production runtime dependency. Future backend changes must replace or adapt this test.
limits: This check evaluates the manifest over a finite candidate set. It is not a complete source archive, wheel contents test, dependency closure analysis or independent install dry run.
Expected missing-pattern warnings concern unrelated candidates deliberately absent from this bounded probe. They are retained in logs.
No peer source implementation changes, package-discovery changes or transport/hardware functionality.
No alternative backend benchmark, hosted execution, whole-product, physical, real-time or accreditation claim.
